implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX and nothing else. Zero ordinary stack arguments is machine-observed: the only PUSH in the body is 0x00641780 PUSH ESI, there is no ADD ESP, and both returns are the one-byte C3 with no immediate (0x006417a1 and 0x006417a5).
implementation.return_note: declared as `Word`, the alias this package's header declares for std::uint32_t, because that is the spelling the definition's own signature carries. It is a full 32-bit word that is exactly 1 or exactly 0. 0x0064179b is MOV EAX,0x1 (bytes B8 01 00 00 00) and 0x006417a2 is XOR EAX,EAX, so no bit of either callee's result is forwarded and no low-byte projection occurs. The machine's register-class phrase for EAX is recorded separately in observed_original_abi.return_semantics and is not a type; the width the machine proves, WIDTH_4_IN_EAX over the complete 19-instruction listing, is 4 bytes and so agrees with the declaration.
implementation.receiver_model: an OPAQUE BYTE RUN and nothing else: `struct alignas(4) AssetData { std::array<std::uint8_t, 0x10> opaque_00_0f{}; }`. No member is named, because the machine-derived receiver record for this VA is `bounds_only: true` (abi_derived.value.receiver: register ECX, offsets [0], max_offset 0, shape R-ALIAS, written_through 0) and that record states how far the body was seen reaching and nothing about which member is which, so a member name would be a layout claim the evidence cannot make. The one displacement the body reads on the receiver is the header constant `kDispatchWordDisplacement` (0x00, from 0x00641783 and 0x0064178e `MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESI]`, whose 8B 06 encoding carries no displacement byte at all), pinned by a static_assert, and the access is `word_at(base, displacement)`. The body reads that word twice (0x00641783 and 0x0064178e) and no other displacement, and stores nothing, so the 0x0c bytes after it are part of the opaque run. The +0x1c sub-object that 0x00641810 and 0x00641820 read is a property of those CALLEES and is deliberately absent.
implementation.dispatch_model: two indirect calls and nothing else, and no struct member anywhere. The receiver's leading word is read as a plain `Word` (a two-level dereference: `MOV EAX,[ESI]` then `MOV EDX,[EAX + disp]`) and the target is a DISPLACEMENT into THAT, reached through `word_through(Word base_word, size_t displacement)`, which takes its base as a Word rather than as a pointer so a one-level reading is not writable at all. Displacement +0x10 (0x00641785) is called first and +0x0c (0x00641790) second, and the second dispatch is decided by the dispatch word as it stands AFTER the first callee has returned. Neither displacement is called a vtable slot as a matter of type: abi_derived.value.dispatch is silent about them (indirect_calls 2, call_offsets [], vtable_shaped_loads 0), so `kSlotCalledFirst` and `kSlotCalledSecond` are header constants for the two byte displacements, each derived as a dword index times kCellWidthBytes and each pinned by a static_assert to the instruction it came from.
implementation.dependency_note: there are no direct callees to declare. The package header declares the cell type (Word (__thiscall*)(AssetData*)) plus four displacement-named accessors -- word_at, store_word, word_through and store_word_through -- and the model test defines two assembly trampolines plus six C++ observers that occupy the cells the model reads, planted through its own `plant(table, index, fn)` helper.

receiver_displacement.0x00: read twice, at 0x00641783 and again at 0x0064178e. It is the DISPATCH WORD: the load is of the receiver's own leading word (ESI = ECX, and there is no LEA, ADD or displacement on ESI anywhere in the 19 instructions), and its value is immediately indexed at 0x00641785 and 0x00641790. mechanics.receiver_writes: none. The 19 instructions contain no store to memory, so the model writes nothing on the receiver and the model test asserts a byte-for-byte match of the receiver block and of both tables around every run.
mechanics.dereference_depth: two. `MOV EAX,[ESI]` loads a POINTER and `MOV EDX,[EAX + 0x10]` then indexes through it. A one-level reading of the same bytes would be `MOV EDX,[ESI + 0x10]`, which is not an instruction in this body.
mechanics.dispatch_word_reread: real and load-bearing. 0x00641783 and 0x0064178e are two independent loads of the same word with a CALL between them and nothing else, so the second dispatch is decided by the value the first callee left behind. The model performs a second load rather than reusing the first, and the model test's case 7 has the first callee overwrite the word and checks that the SECOND table's slot 3 is the one reached.
mechanics.slot_order: fixed by control flow, not by convention: control reaches 0x00641785 before 0x00641790 on every path that gets that far, and the JZ at 0x0064178c exits before the second read is ever reached.
mechanics.zero_test: a 32-bit null test on the WHOLE of EAX, taken-when-zero, not a comparison against 1 and not signed. Any non-zero pattern -- 0x80000000, 0xdeadbeef, 0xffffffff -- takes the fall-through. Both tests share the same false block at 0x006417a2, so there is one false return and not two.
mechanics.control_flow: two conditional branches, both JZ, both with the absolute target 0x006417a2, which is inside the recovered span 0x00641780..0x006417a5. Three basic blocks: entry to 0x0064178c, 0x0064178e to 0x00641799, and the shared false block 0x006417a2..0x006417a5.
mechanics.globals: none. No instruction in the body names a data-segment address, and the model names none.

unresolved_questions: Which concrete functions are reached at table slots 3 and 4? This body names no callee, so the answer is a property of the dispatch word the object carries at run time. It is additionally unsettled by construction: the six tables that install this body do not agree on their slot 3 (0x00641810 in three of them, 0x00dd0b30 in two, 0x00ecc530 in one), so a single answer cannot be right for all six.

Does any real callee in this image ever change the receiver's dispatch word? 0x0064178e proves the model must re-read it; whether the re-read ever matters at run time needs a trace. Static analysis of the candidate callees found no store to a dispatch word, but that is an absence of evidence.

What are the class identity and full layout of the receiver? Only the dispatch word at +0x00 is reachable from this body. The candidate callees 0x00641810, 0x00641820 and 0x00641850 all open with MOV ECX,[ECX + 0x1c] and tail-transfer to a different function, so a +0x1c sub-object almost certainly exists -- but that is read off the CALLEES' bodies, not this one, and it is deliberately absent from the model.

What do the two callees return, a small number or an address? The body tests all 32 bits with TEST EAX,EAX and then produces a fresh 1, so the representation is irrelevant to this reconstruction; the slot return type is modelled as uint32_t for that reason and the question is left to whoever reconstructs the callees.

Does Ghidra have an SDK name for this member that the live cSPAssetDataOTDB this_type set does not list? The set has ten members and this VA is not among them, so the export name stays the canonical VA-embedding form. A name from the ModAPI headers or a vtable-detector pass would settle it; neither was available to this worker.

The C type of the value EAX carries, which no machine record for this VA states and which nothing in this image can settle. The reconstruction declares `Word` (this package's alias for std::uint32_t) because the body itself produces a full 32-bit word and nothing narrows it: 0x0064179b is `MOV EAX,0x1` (bytes B8 01 00 00 00) and 0x006417a2 is `XOR EAX,EAX`, and the two callees' results are consumed whole by `TEST EAX,EAX` and then discarded. The machine side of the record is a register-CLASS classification rather than a type: abi_derived.value.return is {register EAX, register_class integral, type null, void_possible false} and the pack's return_semantics field is null, so the phrase the ABI layer renders is `integral_in_EAX` (the same vocabulary renders `unclassified_in_EAX` for a register it cannot classify, which is not what this record carries). That phrase is recorded in observed_original_abi.return_semantics and is NOT declared as a type anywhere in the source, because it is a description of a register's content in one layer's vocabulary and a typedef named after it would be an artefact rather than a claim. Nothing here can decide the C type: the body has no direct callee, this VA has no outgoing xref row at all, and the two dispatched targets depend on the table the object carries at run time. What IS settled is the WIDTH -- WIDTH_4_IN_EAX over the complete 19-instruction listing -- and `Word` is 4 bytes, so the declaration is as wide as the machine proves the return to be. Whether the original's real signature said `int`, `unsigned int`, `BOOL` or something else remains unknown, and this package does not claim it.
